title: Inverse-limit transport of integral lisse fibres
statement: Under the adic hypotheses, there exists an IntegralFibrePathTransport: for each finite coefficient field E inside Q it supplies a linear path family on the actual integral fibre functor, and its projection to every finite level agrees, after the underlying-set stalk identification, with evaluation of the original finite-set path. Definitions and hypotheses are those of [new-e5-fibre-path-transport-data], [def-pod-lisse-adic-fibre-functors], [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves].

source.place: Weil II (1.1.1) b)-d), pp.146-147; explicit part of the fibre transport argument

proof.text: A finite-type module annihilated by the prescribed power of the uniformizer is a module over the finite quotient ring, hence has finite underlying type. Thus each integral level is a lisse module sheaf.

Apply the all-ring linear family to each finite level. Whisker the resulting natural isomorphisms by the inverse-limit functor. Underlying set naturality supplies compatibility with transition maps; projection naturality proves evaluation. Functoriality of mapIso preserves the four path laws.
